# `Q-5-37` — Brand file not referenced

> The project contains a brand file, but no `brand:` key is set. The
> file is ignored, and your colors, fonts, and logos are not applied.

## What this means

Quarto 1 looks for a brand file automatically. If no `brand:` key is
set, it checks these paths in the project directory:

- `_brand.yml`
- `_brand.yaml`
- `_brand/_brand.yml`
- `_brand/_brand.yaml`

Quarto 2 does not. It applies a brand only when a `brand:` key names
it. This warning fires when one of those files exists and no `brand:`
key is set at the top level or under any `format:` entry.

The render succeeds, but without the brand.

## How to fix

Point `brand:` at the file, in `_quarto.yml`:

```yaml
brand: _brand.yml
```

For a file in a `_brand/` directory, use its path:

```yaml
brand: _brand/_brand.yml
```

To have this added for you, run `qmd-syntax-helper convert -r q-5-37 --in-place <any .qmd in the project>`. It appends the `brand:` line to the project's `_quarto.yml`, choosing the file Quarto 1 would have used. It is not part of `convert --rule all`, because it changes how the project renders.

If the file is not meant to apply to this project, silence the warning:

```yaml
diagnostics:
  Q-5-37: off
```

## Where it is checked

The check runs for each document, on its fully merged metadata. A
`brand:` set anywhere counts: `_quarto.yml`, an active profile, a
`_metadata.yml`, or the document's front matter. It looks only at files in the
project directory, so it also runs for a single file rendered on its own.

`quarto render` prints the warning once, listing the affected documents.
`quarto preview` shows it for the page being previewed. The check does not run
in the browser-based editor, which cannot reliably see non-document project
files.

`qmd-syntax-helper` approximates the same check when it adds the key. It
understands `_quarto.yml`, `_metadata.yml`, and front matter, but not profile
overlays.
